workbookName: Episode Dialog Copy — Craft Wave 2 (35 series)

rows.story_lead: Jane tracks a polar bear across the Arctic with David and Greybeard, from an avalanche start to a garbage dump where the bears eat out of hunger. Scared, she discovers, is what fear is for: a signal to want to come home safely. A voicemail to Dad goes unanswered, so the promised snowmobile ride becomes a lesson about sharing.
rows.resolution: Jane reframes the fear as wanting to come home safely, and understanding the bear comes before rushing in to help her.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. Story detail from the dev set note: avalanche, snowmobile chase, tag-the-polar-bear mission; fear reframed as a safety signal. Content considerations: an avalanche, polar bears forced to eat garbage, vanishing sea ice. Secondary mirrors: the unanswered voicemail to Dad, learning to share. Tail sweep fix-in-place 2026-11-18 (v2.1 + amended register): lead rebuilt fresh from the row's cited evidence; tier unchanged; prior copy replaced, not revised.

rows.story_lead: Tagging a great white shark means a cage dive, and Jane is scared of the animal everyone fears. Marine biologist Carlee Jackson's reframe does its work: sharks bite by mistake, almost never on purpose, and respect beats fear. At home, Tata's paella list shrinks to sustainable choices.
rows.resolution: Respect replaces the fear of sharks, and the groceries follow the lesson home.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. Story detail from the dev set note: cage dive, seal decoy, paella grocery run; the reframe is the coping move. Content considerations: shark-attack talk throughout, nothing on screen. Secondary mirror: Tata's sustainable-seafood lesson.

rows.story_lead: Shrunk to honeybee size, Jane and Greybeard tour the hive until schoolmate Kurtis starts throwing rocks at it. Jadiel takes a sting protecting what he loves. Jane swoops in and tells the truth about bees until even the rock-thrower plants seedballs.
rows.resolution: Anger finds its voice, and standing up for the hive turns an enemy into a helper, because bees sting only to protect their home.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. Story detail from the dev set note: shrink-ship hive visit, Kurtis throws rocks at the hive, Jadiel stung. Content considerations: rocks thrown at a beehive, a child stung, bees vanishing worldwide.

rows.story_lead: Greybeard parachutes into the yard of the neighbor everyone fears, and getting him back means knocking on her door. The feared neighbor turns out to be kind, and the flying-fox lesson lands alongside: when you start to understand a creature, you start to care. A mom's no-shouting-on-work-calls rule gets bent and mended.
rows.resolution: Asking for help saves the lost toy, and the scariest person on the street turns out to be the one who saves him.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. Story detail from the dev set note: parachute drop, Greybeard blown into the feared neighbor's garden. Content considerations: a lost toy who is scared, vampire-bat myths corrected, an endangered species (10,000 to 20,000 flying foxes left).

rows.story_lead: The gharial's bulbed snout is the mystery, but the co-op's chore list comes first, and Jane is impatient with every single one of them. New kid Andre changes the arithmetic at the pool. The answer arrives the way patience works: sideways, after the chores.
rows.resolution: The chores get done first, and the unloved, weird-looking animal gets her help too.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. Story detail from the dev set note: boat capers, co-op chores, new kid Andre, Greybeard falls in the pool. Content considerations: only about 600 gharials left. rows.story_lead: The blue whale's song leads the friends deep into the ocean, and the science mission turns into a rescue when a fishing net catches in the whale's mouth. Jane owns her own yelling out loud, then asks the shy neighbor with the gifted voice to sing. Change happens by listening, then starting a dialogue.
rows.resolution: The apology plus the song free the whale, and talking it out is what carried them there.
rows.evidence_note: Script: Gestdown, identity-checked per the dev set row note (title-card check); confidence high. rows.story_lead: A bug-sized Jane follows a monarch butterfly's road toward Mexico, but the small problem at home gets brushed off by David, and Mr. Patel refuses to plant milkweed. Millie's lost key chain turns out to matter as much as the big mission. Whether it is really small or really large, the monarch scientist says, it all adds up.
rows.resolution: Jane asks for help, the small helps add up exactly as promised, and the not-being-taken-serious feeling dissolves.

A rhino charge nearly tramples them both. Like rhino and oxpecker, they discover they watch each other's backs.
rows.resolution: The argument ends in talking it out, and the partnership comes out stronger for it, the way the vet says symbiosis works.
